neighbours.label: telling one kind of thing from another or identifying it by its features (tell a real coin from a fake, identify a wine, features that characterize a disease), as opposed to the same subjects doing something else
fire: Jewelers can tell a real diamond from a copy with a small lens.
A good cook can tell fresh fish from old fish by smell alone.
Geologists identify a rock by its hardness and the color of its streak.
Birdwatchers learn to distinguish the two warblers by their songs.
The spots on its wings help experts tell this moth from its cousins.
Certain proteins in the blood characterize each type of the infection.
Farmers can identify the breed of a sheep from the shape of its head.
Doctors use a simple test to distinguish a cold from the flu.
quiet: Jewelers can sell a real diamond for a profit in a small shop.
A good cook can keep fresh fish on ice for a day or so.
Geologists carry a rock hammer and a bag of samples up the hill.
Birdwatchers learn to walk quietly through the woods at dawn.
The spots on its wings help this moth hide from its enemies.
Certain proteins in the blood carry oxygen through the body.
Farmers can shear the wool of a sheep in a few minutes.
Doctors use a simple bandage to cover a cut on the hand.

short: telling one kind of thing from another
notes: Output: promotes distinguish, uniquely, distinction, differentiate, distinctive; the - pole fires on 'used to identify' and marks. Probes: tell a coin from a fake 0.50, tell one species from another 0.50, identify a wine's region 0.53, mineral identification 0.56, characterize diseases 0.53, separate two diseases 0.25; carry the crate 0.14, paint each whale 0.09, attract a mate 0.25 on ' to'. 'identify each whale' reached 0.14, 'recognize faces' 0.12, 'sets apart' 0.03 and 'fairly unique' 0.03, so the claim is narrower than the output list suggests.
